message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), water’s freezing (melting) point is lowered relative to the standard 0 °C at 1 atm.  
According to the water phase diagram, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at 10 kPa lies at roughly **–2 °C**.  

So, the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is about **–2 °C** (≈ –3.6 °F).
